cast_dialogue.linea: Rules and remedies, heroes: 'must' obliges, 'can't' forbids, 'should' advises, and 'had better' warns.
At the museum you mustn't touch the paintings, and you can't use flash. But you can take photos without it.
You look terrible, Ben. You should see a doctor, and you'd better rest today.
Can I leave early today? I don't feel well. I have a fever.
If you have a fever, you must drink hot soup and you should stay in bed. Doctor Carmen has spoken!

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Permission: can/can't (informal), may/may not (formal). Obligation: must; prohibition: mustn't or can't. Advice: should/shouldn't; strong advice with warning: had better ('d better). All followed by the infinitive WITHOUT 'to'.

guion: Sofía: Can I take photos in the museum, Ben?
Ben: Yes, but you mustn't use flash. And you can't touch the paintings.
Sofía: Of course. Oh — you don't look well. Do you have a fever?
Ben: A little. I think I should go home.
Sofía: You'd better see a doctor. And you must drink hot soup.
Ben: Yes, doctor Sofía! May I leave my camera here?
Sofía: Sure, but you'd better hurry. The museum closes soon.

reading.texto: The city museum has clear rules: visitors can take photos, but they mustn't use flash, and they can't touch the paintings. Today Ben doesn't feel well — he has a fever. Sofía tells him he should see a doctor and he'd better go home to rest. Abuela Carmen agrees: he must drink hot soup and stay in bed. Rules and advice are different, but both help us live better.
